facts.fact: FAO's GIEWS country brief for Guinea-Bissau says satellite-based data showed some dry spells affected crops in localized areas in 2025, and lists GIEWS Earth Observation for Crop Monitoring among the tools used to prepare it.
facts.system: FAO/GIEWS Earth Observation for Crop Monitoring

facts.fact: WFP Guinea-Bissau says it carries out monthly monitoring of rainy-season conditions, using CHIRPS rainfall, MODIS NDVI and land surface temperature processed in Google Earth Engine, to report vegetation state and flood risk for agriculture.
facts.system: Bulletin de suivi de la saison pluvieuse

facts.fact: WFP Guinea-Bissau states it carries out monthly monitoring of climate conditions and publishes it as a monthly rainy-season bulletin, this issue being August 2025.

facts.fact: The Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia states that members of the multidisciplinary working group following the crop campaign (INM and four agriculture and water directorates) were trained by AGRHYMET on 11-15 August 2026 in satellite imagery, rainfall products, NDVI and yield simulation, to monitor rain and crop state and improve the group's bulletin.
